title: My first game demo ever is up on Steam! Roguelike deckbuilder with 90s arcade aesthetic.
author: MosesSecondofHisName
selftext:
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5212740/Ultimate\_RPS\_Championship/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5212740/Ultimate_RPS_Championship/)

Let me know what you think!

Developed in Unity through using Codex, ChatGPT, Suno, and Firefly.

The thing I learned most while making this was that it was often easier to build a tool within Unity to do what I needed than to learn some new tool or function. The biggest hurdle by far was anchoring and sizing the cosmetics and keeping a consistent aesthetic throughout the game. This was partly handled by developing a visual guide and uploading it to my ChatGPT project docs (I had GPT design a mockup of what I wanted the game to look at then reverse-engineer visual language and rules based on that), but I also made a studio in Unity for the cards and hands to ensure they all had the same base appearance.

I started this project a couple months ago on Codex 5.5 and it's kind of crazy to see what Astra can do now and think about how much easier it would've been to develop if I'd started today.

comments.author: AshlaStudios
comments.body:
Here is my honest opinion:  
  
Way too soon to release this as a demo. 

You need singnificantly more polish, this is pretty much the definition of 'ai slop'. Please don't take it the wrong way.

I like the idea of rock paper sciscors as a simle base for the gameplay loop, being expanded upon with various systems/mechanics. Has potential for sure. But your UI/UX for example is very weak. You'd be surprised by how far you can get with AI if you spend more time on pre production, prepping UI mock ups and feeding them to LLM, iterating on the multiple times to enhance the visuals.

replies.author: MosesSecondofHisName
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback. To be honest, what you described is exactly what I did, so it sounds like I didn't do it quite right. Can you explain a bit more? I don't have any background in UI/UX (which I'm sure is obvious), so if you have any resources you could point me to, I'm all ears.

replies.author: AshlaStudios
replies.body: Take screenshots of your entire UI/UX, all screens, transitions, the entire flow. Paste it into say Astra and also feed it some references from other games which you use as references. Ask for UI/UX feedback, to improve it. Do this simple step as a start and I am sure you'll see there is much to improve.

replies.author: AshlaStudios
replies.body: If you're new to game dev you need to use other games as references and try to replicate specific solutions until it is pretty much the same thing, best way to learn. Then you can iterate.

comments.author: Significant_Treat_87
comments.body:
I agree this is a really cool idea, so good job on that. The really plain sans serif yellow font used throughout is jarring though, because everything else is pixel art and then that font looks like an OS default. 

I also feel like the hand animations are pretty rough considering they’re the main thing you’ll see again and again through the game. I would try to make them more “satisfying”. 

Great job though overall, I think it’s very cool. And sorry, I know you didn’t actually ask for feedback haha.

replies.author: MosesSecondofHisName
replies.body:
No apologies needed, this is AMAZING feedback. Very actionable. I'm gonna start tackling these things now so I can have a better version by launch.

I picked the plain font just for readability because I thought the pixel font would be tough to read the whole time, but you'e right. And you're also right about the animation being lame.

Really, thanks a ton. Looking forward to working on it.
